text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sarajevo press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- President of Bosnia's Moslem-Croat federation, Kresimir Zubak, condemns recent attacks on NATO-led Stabilisation Force (SFOR) in the divided town of Mostar and suggests concrete measures to be undertaken to punish perpetrators.

- Robert Frowick, head of OSCE mission in Bosnia, said in an interview local elections scheduled for July may not be held in disputed town of Brcko, recently placed under international supervision, and southern town of Mostar, where tensions are high due to recent violence.
- The OSCE will carefully supervise the whole electoral process for municipal polls in July, including the registration of voters, Frowick said.
- Bosnia's Serb republic must pay a $12.3 million debt as a condition for Bosnia receiving further gas supplies from Russian gas company, Edhem Bicakcic, Moslem-Croat Federation Prime Ministar says.

- Moslem-Croat federation Defence Minister, Ante Jelavic, refused again to appear before the International Criminal Tribunal for former Yugoslavia, which has asked him to present documents on indicted Croat General Tihomir Blaskic.

- Serbs should be a constituent part of the Moslem-Croat federation, says Mirko Pejanovic, president of the Serb Civic Council. He proposes the federation parliament adopt a constitutional amendment on the issue.

- A factory producing concrete tiles was officially reopned in Blazuj, near Sarajevo, and will initially employ 50 workers and will manufacture 10,000 tiles a day. U.S. company BRF invested one million German marks in the project.

- A report by international police monitors on violent incident this month in Mostar should be a first step towards defusing tensions in the divided town and gaining the upper hand against local mafia, commentary says.
